> Curated papers, systems, and datasets for Text-to-SQL that can recognize ambiguity, ask useful questions, and decline unsupported requests.

Natural-language questions do not always determine one SQL query, and a database cannot answer every request. This collection focuses on how NL2SQL agents detect these situations, resolve them through interaction or additional evidence, and evaluate when to answer or abstain.

[**Explore the interactive catalog →**](https://duyvuleo.github.io/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/) · [Browse papers](papers/README.md) · [Compare benchmarks](docs/benchmark-matrix.md) · [Try the examples](examples/README.md) · [Contribute](CONTRIBUTING.md)

Updated **2026-11-09**. Each paper includes a concise summary, publication status, public sources, and a verification date. Core work and adjacent methods are marked separately. Resource counts include clearly labeled benchmark designs whose artifacts are not yet verified released.

[**Read the detailed paper notes →**](papers/reading-notes.md) for methods, evaluation conditions, findings, limitations and checks against the original text. The index records completed readings and remaining access gaps.

## Scope

We include work that directly studies ambiguity, underspecification, answerability, clarification, or abstention in natural-language querying of relational databases. We also include selected verification, uncertainty, and contextual-grounding methods when their relevance to those problems is explicit. Generic SQL-generation systems and broad agent frameworks belong in the related collections unless they provide a concrete capability relevant to this scope.

An ambiguous request, an unsupported request, a model error, and a valid query returning no rows are different cases. Likewise, a publication, an announced repository, released artifacts, and independently reproduced results are different kinds of evidence. The annotations preserve these distinctions; inclusion is not a deployment endorsement.

| 2026 | [Boundary-Aware NL2SQL: Integrating Reliability through Hybrid Reward and Data Synthesis](papers/README.md#bar-sql)<br>arXiv preprint<br><em>core</em> | Trains SQL generation, clarification, missing-constraint follow-up and refusal with mutated enterprise examples, supervised fine-tuning and task-specific reinforcement-learning rewards. Ent-SQL-Bench combines SQL execution agreement with LLM-judged natural-language responses. Evidence comes from a held-out portion of the authors&#x27; synthetic enterprise corpus; response-level clarification scores do not establish successful multi-turn resolution or transfer to unseen domains. | [Code](https://github.com/TianSongS/BAR-SQL) · [Data](https://github.com/TianSongS/BAR-SQL/tree/main/benchmark)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#bar-sql)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/bar-sql.md) |
| 2021 | [NL-EDIT: Correcting Semantic Parse Errors through Natural Language Interaction](papers/README.md#nl-edit)<br>NAACL 2021<br><em>adjacent</em> | Predicts clause-level SQL edits from feedback, explanations and schema context, using synthetic pretraining and SPLASH. One-turn correction improves, but 16.93% of test examples gain errors. Its representation/evaluation ignores condition values and restricts subquery structure; structural progress does not guarantee semantic preservation or faster multi-turn convergence. Cross-parser gains decrease with stronger base parsers. | [Code](https://github.com/MSR-LIT/NLEdit) · [Data](https://github.com/MSR-LIT/NLEdit/tree/main/data)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#nl-edit)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/nl-edit.md) |
| 2020 | [Speak to your Parser: Interactive Text-to-SQL with Natural Language Feedback](papers/README.md#splash)<br>ACL 2020<br><em>adjacent</em> | Pairs Spider parser errors with explanations and short human correction feedback to evaluate one-round parse repair. Correction uses exact set match; end-to-end scores are derived from initial successes and explanation-supported failures. The reported human ceiling estimates feedback completeness, not observed human SQL repair. Fully specified inputs distinguish this task from ambiguity detection and autonomous clarification. | [Data](https://github.com/MSR-LIT/Splash)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#splash)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/splash.md) |
| 2026 | [SQLStructEval: Structural Evaluation of LLM Text-to-SQL Generation](papers/README.md#sqlstructeval)<br>Findings of IJCNLP-AACL 2026<br><em>adjacent</em> | Measures canonical SQL-structure variation across repeated generations and input perturbations. A full JSON-to-SQL pipeline improves execution accuracy and correct-output concentration while increasing overall diversity. Metrics also reflect parse coverage; structural variation is not itself error. Selected error-case analyses are not population rates, and the notes flag an inconsistent COUNT(1) label in the pipeline illustration. | [Code](https://github.com/XanderZhou2022/AACL2026-SQLSTRUCTEVAL)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#sqlstructeval)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/sqlstructeval.md) |

SQL experiments use reference-execution labels and random in-domain train/test splits on Spider, Spider-Realistic and BIRD. Calibration gains are stronger than selection/discrimination gains; matched sampling, labeled examples and untested distribution-shift behavior limit deployment claims. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#simba-uq)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/simba-uq.md) |

Support varies with model, dataset and similarity definition. SQL correctness is labeled by reference-result agreement on the supplied database; consistency is not a semantic proof or a diagnosis of request answerability. | Release not verified<br>[Details](papers/README.md#consistency-hypothesis)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/consistency-hypothesis.md) |
| 2026 | [Auditing and Repairing LLM-as-Judge Failures in a Production Text-to-SQL Pipeline](papers/README.md#synca-audit)<br>EMNLP 2026 Industry Track<br><em>adjacent</em> | Audits SQL-faithfulness judges using distinct enriched, random and active-disagreement samples, then compares replacements and selective routing. Unanimity gains apply to retained cases, and the Qwen–Opus accuracy comparison is inconclusive. One-domain gold and deferred data limit transfer/reproduction; unreconciled appendix cost and count arithmetic preclude treating precise savings or population estimates as established. | [Code](https://github.com/JamesL404/synca-audit)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#synca-audit)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/synca-audit.md) |
| 2026 | [Text-to-SQL Models Make Choices Without Saying So](papers/README.md#specbridge)<br>arXiv preprint<br><em>core</em> | Builds 204 controlled request triples on 12 existing databases to separate computing an interpretation from disclosing a calculation choice. Models often compute both specific versions but return one for the open request; deciding before separate generation and preserving wording improve coverage. Tests cover one choice/two references, score precision on clear requests, and use simulated users and reconstructed product baselines. | [Code](https://github.com/Xyc-arch/specbridge-artifact) · [Data](https://github.com/Xyc-arch/specbridge-artifact/tree/main/benchmark)<br>[Details](papers/README.md#specbridge)<br>[Reading notes](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/blob/main/papers/notes/specbridge.md) |

## Contributing

Suggest a resource or correction through an [issue](https://github.com/duyvuleo/awesome-reliable-text-to-sql/issues/new/choose) or pull request. Include a primary source and explain the connection to ambiguity or unanswerability. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the entry format and checks.

The canonical records are [papers.json](data/papers.json) and [resources.json](data/resources.json). The indexes are generated, so contributors only need to maintain one record per work.
